paper_metadata.title: Investigation of Multiple Frequency Ranges Using Discrete Wavelet Decomposition of Resting-State Functional Connectivity in Mild Traumatic Brain Injury Patients

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and describes the source population. However, it uses a convenience sample from a larger imaging protocol without specifying the total number of eligible patients screened versus those enrolled, making it difficult to assess the participation rate and potential selection bias.

items.evidence_snippet: Thirty-two mTBI patients (41.7 – 17.1 years, 21M:11F) were prospectively recruited as part of a larger imaging protocol... Thirty-one neurologically intact subjects (37.3 – 17.1 years, 17M:14F) served as a control population.
items.reasoning: The authors define the age, sex, and clinical status (mTBI vs. control) of the participants.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (functional connectivity) was measured using objective fMRI data with standardized preprocessing and wavelet decomposition. The same protocol was applied to all participants.
